I’ll use the crimes codebase-risk skill to trace both names and check the rename’s scope without changing files.


The domain concept is **a tenant**, called **`team` in Python** and **`workspace` in TypeScript**. Crimes suggests **`organization`** as a common name; that is a recommendation, not an established project decision.

I ran crimes 0.29.1 `context` on all three source files with `--root . --format json --no-skill-update` and inspected their contents. No files were changed.

| Location | Current names and rename scope |
|---|---|
| [API routes](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10) | `get_team`, `create_team`, `team_seats`, `change_team_plan`; `team_id` parameters and references; four `/api/teams…` routes. |
| [Plan definitions](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10) | The `Plan` docstring describes a “team.” `Plan.TEAM = "team"` is a **billing tier**, so it must not be blindly replaced during the object rename. |
| [Web client](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:12) | `Workspace`, return types, `getWorkspace`, `createWorkspace`, `workspaceSeats`, `changeWorkspacePlan`, comments and the filename. URLs currently mix `/api/workspaces` and `/api/teams`. |

The rename crosses an HTTP boundary, so changing identifiers alone would leave the product inconsistent. These contracts also need attention:

- **Creation path:** the client sends `POST /api/workspaces`; the backend declares `POST /api/teams`.
- **Plan-change method:** the client sends `PUT`; the backend declares `POST`.
- **Additional URL issues found by reading source:** `getWorkspace` constructs `/api/workspaces/` plus the ID, which the literal-path detector misses. Seat and plan requests send literal `:id` strings instead of interpolating their `id` argument.
- **Plan values already diverge:** Python has `free`, `pro`, `team`, `scale`; TypeScript has `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`. This is the highest-severity finding and requires a separate contract decision. Python’s module describes its list as canonical.
- **Network behavior:** crimes flags `getWorkspace` because it calls `fetch`. Inspection confirms network I/O, but does not establish a server-side mutation.

For an `organization` rename, the coordinated scope would include the three files above, exported types/functions, client filename and any importers, documentation, and both sides of the route contract. Existing external clients would need a migration decision if URLs change. Tests should cover get/create/seats/plan requests and agreed plan values.

All three context reports returned `analysis_status: complete`, but discovered **no likely tests**; test coverage remains unknown. Crimes excluded three JSON files and one TOML file. I inspected those manually and found no additional domain-name references. No additional callers or test files were present in this fixture; zero reported import blast radius does not establish that external HTTP consumers are unaffected.
